376111.title: Matching upper-bound conjecture for the linear Turán number of the four-edge hypertree
376111.literal_statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ and let $P_4^r$ denote the four-edge $r$-uniform hypertree considered in the paper. For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$, write $ex_r^{\mathrm{lin}}(n,P_4^r)$ for the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex linear $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $P_4^r$.

**The $P_4^r$ upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
ex_r^{\mathrm{lin}}(n,P_4^r) \leq \dfrac{(r+1)n}{r}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if the linear $r$-uniform hypergraph is the union of disjoint Steiner systems $S(2,r,r^2)$, given that the Steiner system $S(2,r,r^2)$ exists.

The conjecture would provide a matching upper bound for the lower bound established under the assumptions that $r^2\mid n$ and that $S(2,r,r^2)$ exists. The authors note that the corresponding result is known for $r\in\{2,3\}$, while obtaining the general upper bound is substantially more difficult.

376304.title: Two-barrier Ore-degree conjecture for direct-sum matchings
376304.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with $q$ elements, and let $\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{k}$ denote the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $V$. For a family $\mathcal F\subsetneq\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{k}$, let $\sigma_{k,q}(\mathcal F)$ be its projective Ore-degree and let $\nu_{\oplus}(\mathcal F)$ be its maximum direct-sum matching size. For integers $k\ge2$, $s\ge2$, and $n\ge ks$, define $D_q(n,k,s-1)$ as in the paper.

**Two-barrier Ore-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\sigma_{k,q}(\mathcal F)>\max\left\{\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q}D_q(n,k,s-1),\;\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{\max\{0,(s+1)k-n-1\}}{1}_{q}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{sk-2}{k-1}_{q}\right\},
$$

then $\nu_{\oplus}(\mathcal F)\ge s$.

This corrects the single-threshold formulation, which fails in the full range because both the linear-stability obstruction and the subspace-clique obstruction can control the Ore-degree threshold.

367084.title: The complete-intersection conjecture for t-intersecting spanning trees
367084.literal_statement:
Let $F_{n,\ell}$ be a spanning forest on $n$ vertices with $\ell$ edges, whose components have either $k$ or $k+1$ vertices, with component sizes as equal as possible. Let $\mathcal{F}_{n,t,j}$ be the family of all spanning trees that contain at least $t+j$ of the $t+2j$ edges of $F_{n,t+2j}$. A family of spanning trees is **$t$-intersecting** if any two trees in it have at least $t$ edges in common.

**Complete-intersection conjecture.** For any $t$ and $n$, there exists a $j$ such that $\mathcal{F}_{n,t,j}$ is the largest $t$-intersecting set of spanning trees.

This conjecture is presented as a “Complete Intersection Theorem”-type statement, extending the comparison between fixed-edge constructions and families requiring many edges from a balanced spanning forest. The supplied status evidence says that the conjecture has since been proved by Elizaveta Iarovikova and Andrey Kupavskii.

367365.title: Rank characterization conjecture for the $(k,d)$-volume rigidity matroid
367365.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a $k$-dimensional simplicial complex on vertex set $X_0$, with $X_1$ its set of edges and $X_k$ its set of $k$-faces. For disjoint families of sets ${\cal A},{\cal B}$, let $H_{{\cal A},{\cal B}}$ be the bipartite graph with vertex set ${\cal A}\cup{\cal B}$ and an edge between $A$ and $B$ exactly when $A\subset B$. Let $\nu(G)$ denote the matching number of a graph $G$, and let an edge set $E\subset X_1$ be independent in the standard $d$-rigidity matroid when it is independent in that matroid. **Rank characterization conjecture.** Let $d\ge 3$, $1\le k\le d-1$, and let $X$ be a $k$-dimensional simplicial complex on $n\ge d+2$ vertices. Then

$$
\operatorname{rank}({\cal M}_{k,d}(X))=\max_{E} \nu(H_{E,X_k}),
$$

where the maximum is taken over all $E\subset X_1$ that are independent in the standard $d$-rigidity matroid. This would characterize the rank of the $(k,d)$-volume rigidity matroid in terms of the standard $d$-rigidity matroid of the $1$-skeleton. The statement is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is given in the source.

367689.title: The maximum partial-dual genus bound for planar graphs
367689.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $G^c$ denote its complement, let $\chi(G^c)$ be the chromatic number of $G^c$, and let $y_G$ denote the maximum genus among partial duals of $G$. For an integer $\lambda$, say that $G$ is **$\lambda$-edge-connected** if every edge cut of $G$ has size at least $\lambda$.

**Maximum partial-dual genus conjecture.** If $G\not\cong C_3$ is a $\lambda$-edge-connected planar graph with $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$, then

$$
y_G\leq 2\chi(G^c)-\lambda+1.
$$

This conjecture proposes a chromatic-number bound for the maximum partial-dual genus in the cases of 1- and 2-edge-connected planar graphs, where the authors report that they have not found graphs attaining the previously obtained bound. The even paths and even cycles discussed immediately before the conjecture satisfy the proposed inequality.

370754.title: Spectral stability conjecture for minimum $Q$-degree hypergraphs
370754.literal_statement:
Let $p>1$, $s\geq r\geq2$, let $Q$ be an $s$-vertex $r$-graph, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of $r$-graphs with $\pi(Q,\overline{\mathcal{F}})>0$. For $n$ vertices, let $\mathcal{G}_{n}$ be the collection of all $n$-vertex $\mathcal{F}$-free $r$-graphs with minimum $Q$-degree at least

$$
(1-\varepsilon)\pi(Q,\overline{\mathcal{F}})\binom{n}{s-1},
$$

and define

$$
\lambda^{(p)}(Q,\mathcal{G}_{n})=\max\{\lambda^{(p)}(Q,G):G\in\mathcal{G}_{n}\}.
$$

**The spectral stability conjecture.** There exists $n_{0}$ such that for any $\mathcal{F}$-free $r$-graph $H$ on $n\geq n_{0}$ vertices,

$$
\lambda^{(p)}(Q,H)\leq\lambda^{(p)}(Q,\mathcal{G}_{n}).
$$

Moreover, if equality holds, then $H\in\mathcal{G}_{n}$. The paper presents this as a proposed extension of its spectral stability theorem, obtained by removing an additional minimum-degree condition; no resolution is supplied in the given text.

371286.title: The bipartite unique domination bound
371286.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple bipartite graph without isolated vertices, with order $n=|V|$ and domination number $\gamma(G)=\gamma$. A **unique minimum dominating set** is a minimum dominating set of $G$ that is the only one. Define

$$
\Phi(n,\gamma)=\max\left(0,n-3\gamma-2\left\lceil\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rceil-\left\lfloor\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rfloor+1\right).
$$

**Bipartite unique domination bound.** If $G$ has a unique minimum dominating set, $\gamma\geq 2$, and $n\geq 3\gamma$, then its size $s(G)$ is bounded above by

$$
m(n,\gamma)=2\gamma+2\left\lceil\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rceil\left\lfloor\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rfloor+\min\left\\{n-3\gamma,2\left\lceil\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rceil-\left\lfloor\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rfloor+1\right\\}\left(2\left\lceil\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rceil+1\right)+\sum_{i=1}^{\Phi}\left(2\left\lceil\frac{\gamma}{2}\right\rceil+1+\left\lceil\frac{i}{2}\right\rceil\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes the sharp edge bound for bipartite graphs with a unique minimum dominating set in the stated range, refining the general bounds for uniquely dominatable graphs and complementing known results for special cases such as domination number $2$.

372295.title: Extremal formula for Berge-disjoint paths
372295.literal_statement:
Let $\ell,r$ be integers and let $k\geq 2$. Write

$$
\ell'=\left\lfloor\frac{\ell+1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

For an $r$-uniform hypergraph, let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\text{Berge-} kP_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex hypergraph containing no Berge copy of $k$ vertex-disjoint paths of length $\ell$. **The extremal formula for Berge-disjoint paths.** There exists $N_{\ell,r,k}$ such that, whenever $n>N_{\ell,r,k}$ and $2\leq r\leq k\left\lfloor\frac{\ell+1}{2}\right\rfloor$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\text{Berge-} kP_\ell)=\binom{k\ell'-1}{r-1}(n-k\ell'-1+1)+\binom{k\ell'-1}{r}+\mathbb{I}_r\binom{k\ell'-1}{r-2}.
$$

Here $\mathbb{I}_r$ is the indicator appearing in the stated formula. The conjecture proposes that the proved extremal result remains valid throughout the indicated wider range of $r$; the source notes that the lower bound follows from a similar construction, while the upper bound remains to be established.

362021.title: Regularity formula for t-path ideals of unicyclic graphs
362021.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple graph having at most one cycle $C$ of length $m$. Let $t\geq 2$ be a natural number. Write $S$ for the polynomial ring associated with $G$, $I_t(G)$ for its $t$-path ideal, $\nu_t(G)$ for the maximum number of pairwise suitable $t$-paths in $G$, and call $G$ **$t$-proximal** when it satisfies the corresponding $t$-proximity condition. Then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(G))=\begin{cases}
(t-1)\nu_t(G)+\left(\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(C))-(t-1)\nu_3(C)\right), & \text{if }G\text{ is }t\text{-proximal},\\
(t-1)\nu_t(G), & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Regularity conjecture for t-path ideals.** The displayed formula should hold. In particular,

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(G))=(t-1)\nu_t(G)
$$

when $G$ is a tree. This conjecture is presented as a natural generalization of the paper's theorem for $3$-path ideals; the supplied text gives no resolution status for the general $t$-path statement.

366209.title: Gir2o–Snyder–Popielarz linear out-degree conjecture for linked tournaments
366209.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A tournament is a complete graph with exactly one orientation assigned to each edge. A digraph is **$k$-linked** if every $2k$-tuple of distinct vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_k,y_1,\ldots,y_k$ can be joined by $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths, with the $i$th path starting at $x_i$ and ending at $y_i$. Let $\delta^+(D)$ denote the minimum out-degree of a tournament $D$.

**Gir2o–Snyder–Popielarz conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that every $(2k+1)$-connected tournament with minimum out-degree at least $Ck$ is $k$-linked.

The source reports this as an unresolved conjecture. Its significance is that the paper proves the same connectivity condition with a polynomial minimum out-degree bound, while the conjecture asks for a linear bound in $k$.

366300.title: Lin–Miao–Guo conjecture on the maximum $A_{\alpha}$-spread
366300.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple undirected graph with $n\geq 5$ vertices. Let $A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal degree matrix, $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix, and $\alpha\in[0,1]$. If $\lambda_1^{(\alpha)}(G)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(G)$ are respectively the largest and smallest eigenvalues of $A_{\alpha}(G)$, define the **$A_{\alpha}$-spread** by

$$
S_{\alpha}(G)=\lambda_1^{(\alpha)}(G)-\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(G).
$$

**Lin–Miao–Guo conjecture.** If $1/2\leq\alpha<1$, then

$$
S_{\alpha}(G)\leq S_{\alpha}(Ki_{n,n-1}),
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong Ki_{n,n-1}$.

This conjecture proposes the extremal connected graph for the $A_{\alpha}$-spread when $\alpha$ is at least one half. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved; the notation $Ki_{n,n-1}$ is used in the source but is not defined in the provided context.

366396.title: Turánability conjecture for oriented graphs
366396.literal_statement:
Let $D_r$ be the tournament on $3r$ vertices obtained from the $r$-blow-up of the directed cycle $C_3$ by replacing each of its three independent sets with a transitive tournament. An oriented graph $H$ is **Turánable** if there exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n\geq n_0$ vertices with minimum semi-degree $\delta^0(G)\geq \lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ contains $H$ as a subgraph. The **Turánability conjecture for oriented graphs.** An oriented graph $H$ is Turánable if and only if there is an $r\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
H\subseteq D_r.
$$

This would extend the Bollobás–Häggkvist characterization from tournaments to all oriented graphs. The source states it as a belief after proving the corresponding result for powers of cycles, and gives no resolution, so it remains open.

357156.title: Largest cyclic critical group conjecture for arithmetical structures on star and complete graphs
357156.literal_statement:
Let $a_1=1$ and $a_n=a_{n-1}^2+a_{n-1}$ for $n\geq 2$. For an arithmetical structure on the star graph $S_n$ or the complete graph $K_n$, its critical group is a finite abelian group; a cyclic critical group is one isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ for some positive integer $m$. The construction considered has critical group $\mathbb{Z}/a_{n-1}\mathbb{Z}$. **Largest cyclic critical group conjecture.** For $n\geq 4$, the largest cyclic group that can be realized as a critical group of an arithmetical structure on $S_n$ or on $K_n$ is

$$
\mathbb{Z}/a_{n-1}\mathbb{Z}.
$$

The preceding construction realizes this cyclic critical group using the Sylvester-sequence arithmetical structure. The conjecture asserts that no arithmetical structure on either graph realizes a cyclic critical group of larger order for $n\geq 4$.

358614.title: Polynomial compressibility of bounded clique-number acyclic oriented graphs
358614.literal_statement:
For $k \geq 3$, let $\mathcal A_k$ be the family of all acyclic oriented graphs with absolute clique number at most $k$, and let $\mathcal R_k$ be the family of all acyclic oriented graphs with relative clique number at most $k$. An **o-clique** is an oriented graph in which every two vertices are joined by a directed path of length at most $2$. The absolute oriented clique number $\omega_{ao}(H)$ is the maximum size of an o-clique contained in $H$, while the relative oriented clique number $\omega_{ro}(H)$ is the maximum size of a subset $S\subseteq V(H)$ such that every two vertices of $S$ are joined in $H$ by a directed path of length at most $2$.

**Polynomial compressibility conjecture.** For $k \geq 3$, the families $\mathcal A_k$ and $\mathcal R_k$ are polynomially $\tau$-bounded.

This would give polynomial bounds on the compressibility parameter for these families of acyclic oriented graphs. The supplied text does not state whether the claim has been resolved.

360261.title: Heng et al.'s conjecture on infinite families of 1-MDS codes
360261.literal_statement:
Throughout this section, let $q=2^h$ with $h\geq 3$, let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_q$, and write $\alpha_i=\alpha^i$ for $1\leq i\leq q-1$. For $3\leq k\leq q-2$, define

$$
M_k=\left[\begin{array}{ccccc}
1&1&\cdots&1&1\\
\alpha_1&\alpha_2&\cdots&\alpha_{q-2}&\alpha_{q-1}\\
\alpha_1^2&\alpha_2^2&\cdots&\alpha_{q-2}^2&\alpha_{q-1}^2\\
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\
\alpha_1^{k-2}&\alpha_2^{k-2}&\cdots&\alpha_{q-2}^{k-2}&\alpha_{q-1}^{k-2}\\
\alpha_1^k&\alpha_2^k&\cdots&\alpha_{q-2}^k&\alpha_{q-1}^k
\end{array}\right],
$$

and let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the $q$-ary linear code generated by the rows of $M_k$. A linear code with parameters $[n,k,d]_q$ is called **1-MDS** when its minimum distance is one less than the Singleton bound, namely $d=n-k$.

**Heng et al.'s conjecture.** For each $3\leq k\leq q-2$, the linear code $\mathcal{C}_k$ is a $1$-MDS $[q-1,k,q-k-1]_q$ code, and the minimum-weight codewords of both $\mathcal{C}_k$ and its dual $\mathcal{C}_k^{\perp}$ support $2$-designs.

This conjecture proposes an infinite family of near-MDS-type codes arising from a matrix whose full-rank minors are governed by zero-sum subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$. It remains open in the supplied source, which attributes the conjecture to Heng et al.

360775.title: Improved minimal-filling bound for irreducible cycles in simplicial complexes
360775.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional simplicial complex in which every $(d-1)$-face is contained in at most $\Delta$ different $d$-faces. Let $c\in Z_{d-1}(X,\mathbb{F}_2)$ be an irreducible cycle, meaning that whenever $c=c_1+c_2$ with $c_1$ and $c_2$ having disjoint supports, either $c_1=0$ or $c_2=0$. Define its minimum filling size by

$$
m(c)=\min\{\lvert\operatorname{supp}(f)\rvert:f\in C_d(X,\mathbb{F}_2),\ \partial f=c\},
$$

and call an element attaining this minimum a minimal filling. **Minimal-filling conjecture.** There exists a constant $c(d)<1$ such that the number of minimal fillings of $c$ is at most

$$
O\left((c(d)\Delta)^{m(c)}\right).
$$

This proposes an improvement over the general shortest-path counting phenomenon to higher-dimensional simplicial complexes; the source gives no resolution of the claim.

354350.title: Maximum spectral radius conjecture for odd-cycle-free non-bipartite graphs
354350.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges. For integers $k\ge 1$, let $S_{2k-1}(K_{s,t})$ be obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ by replacing an edge with a path $P_{2k+1}$, introducing $2k-1$ new vertices. Its odd girth is $2k+3$.

**Maximum spectral radius conjecture.** If $G$ contains no member of $\{C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2k+1}\}$ and is non-bipartite, then

$$
\lambda(G)\leq \lambda\left(S_{2k-1}\left(K_{2,\frac{m-2k+1}{2}}\right)\right),
$$

with equality if and only if $m$ is odd and $G=S_{2k-1}\left(K_{2,\frac{m-2k+1}{2}}\right)$.

The conjecture proposes the extremal non-bipartite graph for the largest spectral radius under the prescribed odd-cycle exclusions; the paper notes that its methods support the claim for progressively longer forbidden odd cycles, but the general assertion remains open.

355274.title: The four-color bound for locally irregular edge colorings of colorable graphs
355274.literal_statement:
All graphs in this paper are finite and simple. A graph is **locally irregular** if the degrees of the endpoints of every edge are distinct. A locally irregular edge coloring is an edge coloring in which every color class induces a locally irregular subgraph. A graph is **colorable** if it admits such a coloring, and for a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a locally irregular edge coloring.

**Four-color bound.** Every colorable connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)\leq 4.
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of the refuted Local Irregularity Conjecture, motivated by the bow-tie graph, which requires four colors. The supplied text does not establish whether the four-color bound is proved or remains open.

355998.title: Equality of rational blowdown depth and combinatorial depth
355998.literal_statement:
Let $W_{p,q}(\mathbf{n})$ denote the minimal symplectic filling of $(L(p,q),\xi_{can})$ corresponding to $\mathbf{n}=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)$ in the parameterizing set $\mathcal{Z}_k(\frac{p}{p-q})$. For $k\geq 3$, define $\operatorname{dpt}(\mathbf{n})$ to be the number of entries equal to $1$ in the interior of $\mathbf{n}$:

$$
\operatorname{dpt}(\mathbf{n})=\left|\{i\mid 1<i<k\text{ and }n_i=1\}\right|.
$$

The **rational blowdown depth conjecture.** The rational blowdown depth of $W_{p,q}(\mathbf{n})$ is equal to $\operatorname{dpt}(\mathbf{n})$.

The preceding result gives only the upper bound by $\operatorname{dpt}(\mathbf{n})$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is always sharp, so the minimum number of successive symplectic rational blowdowns needed to obtain the filling from the minimal resolution is determined by the interior entries equal to $1$.

349310.title: Longest arithmetic progressions in generalised Thue–Morse sequences
349310.literal_statement:
Let $p,q,n\in\mathbb{N}^{+}$, set $Q=p+q$, and let $A_{p,q}(d)$ denote the maximum length of an arithmetic progression of difference $d$ occurring in the generalised Thue–Morse sequence associated with parameters $p,q$. Assume $n>2$. **Longest-progression conjecture.**

$$
\max_{d\leqslant Q^n+1}A_{p,q}(d)=\begin{cases} A_{p,q}(Q^n-1)=Q^n+Q+2, & \text{if }p=q=1\text{ and }n\text{ is even},\\ A_{p,q}(Q^n-1)=Q^n+Q, & \text{if }p=q>1\text{ and }n\text{ is even},\\ A_{p,q}(Q^n+1)=Q^n+Q, & \text{if }p=q=1\text{ and }n\text{ is odd},\\ A_{p,q}(Q^n+1)=Q^n+Q-1, & \text{if }q>p=1\text{ or }p>q=1,\\ A_{p,q}(Q^n+1)=Q^n+Q-2, & \text{if }p,q>1\text{ and }p\ne q\text{ or }n\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}
$$

The preceding results establish the relevant long progressions for differences $Q^n+1$, and for differences $Q^n-1$ when $p=q$; the conjecture asserts that no longer progression occurs for any difference up to $Q^n+1$.
